χααναία.definition: priest's robe, J.AJ3.7.1 : a mistranslation of Aram. kāhǎnayyâ 'priests'

χαλαίπους.definition: neut. gen. loose, trailing feet, halting, Nic.Th.458; vv.ll

χάλις.definition: neat wine, Hippon.73, Docum. ant; f.l. for Them.Or.23.297a

χαλκίς.definition: an unknown bird; = pica maritima , Gloss

χάμψα.definition: Egyptian name for Hdt.2.69, cj. in A.Supp.878

χάος.definition: Att. chaos, the first state of; space, the expanse of air, B.5.27, cf. Ar.Nu.424 , 627, Av.1218

χαρακτήρ.definition: engraver, Euryph. ap; graving tool, Daimachus4J. ap.St.Byz. s.v

χαρίτιον.definition: in form = Lat.fimirium or fimarium, Gloss

χάρμη.definition: prop. joy of battle, lust of battle; = Stesich.94, Ibyc.62, Pi.Dith.3.13

χάρων.definition: as pr. n., Charon, the ferryman of the Styx, E.Alc.254 , 361, al.; voc. Cratin.324c ; but Ar.Ra.184

χαυνότης.definition: porousness, sponginess; looseness of a bandage, Gal. ap.Orib.46.1.15

χείμαρος.definition: plug in a ship's bottom, drawn out when the ship was brought on land, to let out the bilge- water, Hes.Op.626

χειμών.definition: the wintry quarter of the heavens, the north, Hdt.2.26; metaph., storm of calamity sent by the gods, A.Pr.643; ib.1015, cf. Ch.202 , 1066 ; . . in the storm of battle, S.Ant.670; . . of the madness of Ajax, Id.Aj.207 …

χείρ.definition: dual pl. penult. being regularly short, when the ult. is long; dat. pl. regularly , 2942c : but Poets used the penult. long or short in all cases, as the verse required, ; gen. dual S.El.206 , 1394 , IG22.1498.76; gen…

χέλυς.definition: tortoise, h.Merc.33; the constellation Lyra, Arat.268

χέλυσμα.definition: sheathing like the shell of a tortoise, to protect the lower part of a ship during haulage, Thphr.HP5.7.2

χερείων.definition: of things, 'tis not the worse part, 'twere not amiss, Od.17.176, cf. 23.262

χεριάρης.definition: skilled in fitting with the hand, dexterous, Pi.P.5.35

χεῦμα.definition: that which is poured, stream; generally, fall of snow, Nonn.D.3.213, cf. 210

χίραμα.definition: a disease in horses' feet, Hippiatr.52

χλανίς.definition: upper-garment of wool, finer than; later, = 3, Lat. paludamentum, Jul.ad Ath.274c, 278d

χλῆδος.definition: slime, mud, the rubbish carried down by a flood or swept out of a house, A.Fr.16, D.55.22, 27: metaph., Crates Com.28

χλόος.definition: greenish-yellow or light green colour: hence, pallor, A. R.2.1216, cf. 3.298, Nic.Al.570, 579; Call.Aet.3.1.12; contr. Hp. ap. Gal.19.155

χλωρότης.definition: greenness, Plu.Flam.3; pale colour, of gold mixed with silver, Plu.2.952c; pallor, ib.395c

χοή.definition: pouring out of liquid, drink-offering; rarely of libations in general, S.OC469, 1599

χοηφόρος.definition: offering to the dead; a Tragedy by A., in which the Chorus pours to the shade of Agamemnon

χοῖνιξ.definition: choenix, a dry measure, esp. for; from the likeness of shape, a kind of stocks for fastening the legs, Ar.Pl.276, D.18.129

χόριον.definition: membrane that encloses the foetus in the; membrane round the inside of the egg, Arist.GA754a1

χόριος.definition: in Tactics, a form of Ael.Tact.27.1, 28.3, Arr.Tact.23.1, 24.3

χορός.definition: choir, band of dancers and singers, h. Ven.118, Pi.N.5.23, Fr.199; Ev.Luc.15.25

χρεώ.definition: Ep. gen. less freq. neut; used by Hom. ellipt., c. acc. pers., ; Od.1.225, Il.10.85: folld. by a gen., need of it touches me not, 9.608; 10.43, cf. 9.75; 11.606: also c. inf., he needs must stand firm, ib.409; Od.4.70…

χρόνος.definition: time, Hom. , etc.: dist. fr; time in the abstract, Timo 76; S.E.M.10.197, cf. Plu.2.153b; defined by Zeno Stoic.1.26, Apollod. ib.3.260

χρύσαφος.definition: a kind of fish, perh. gilt head, Marc.Sid.12

χρυσίς.definition: a vessel of gold, piece of gold; gold-broidered dress, Luc.Nigr.11: pl., gold- embroidered shoes, Id.D Deor.2.2

χρωστήρ.definition: that which colours or dyes: a lead-pencil, AP6.68

χύσις.definition: shedding, pouring out or; diffusion, e.g. of nutriment, Gal.6.87; opp. Id.Nat.Fac.1.3 ; coupled with Chrysipp.Stoic.2.136, cf. 188

χῶρος.definition: like I, a definite space, piece of; space, compass, Plb.11.1.3

χωροφύλαξ.definition: guard or watcher of a country or place, Gloss., dub. in CIG5040

χῶσις.definition: heaping up, esp. of earth, raising a; filling up, blocking by carth thrown in, Id.3.2; D.H.5.41

χάζω.definition: cause to retire; Act. only in Hsch. and in compd; c. gen., draw back or retire from, Il.12.172; 11.504; 15.426; 11.539; 13.193, cf. 17.357; less freq. with a Prep., 16.122; 13.153; nor in truth was he far from the man…

χαιρηδών.definition: delectation, Com. word in Ar.Ach.4, formed after

χαίρω.definition: Il.7.191, etc.; 3pl. imper. E.HF575: impf., Ep. Il.14.156, Ion. 18.259: fut. 20.363, Hdt.1.128, Ar.Pl.64, And.1.101, Arr.An.5.20.6; Ep. redupl. inf. Il.15.98; later v.l. in Apoc.11.10: aor. Plu.Luc.25: pf. Ar.V.764, p…

χάλαζα.definition: any small knot like a hailstone; pimple or tubercle in the flesh of swine, Arist.HA603b18, Pr.963b34, Androsth. ap. Ath.3.93c

χαλαρόω.definition: in Pass., to be relaxed in tension, Erot. s.v

χάλασις.definition: slackening, loosening, of; free play of the parts of a whole, Plot.4.4.45; Dam.Pr.47

χάλασμα.definition: slackened condition, relaxation; gap in the line of battle, Plb.18.30.8; to be packed not too tightly, Plu.Aem.32

χαλδαΐζω.definition: follow the Chaldaean fashion or creed, Ph.1.581,2.11

χαλεπαίνω.definition: mostly of persons, to be violent, angry, Il.19.183, cf. Ar.Ra.1020 , Th.3.82, 8.92, Pl.R.426e, etc.; display or portray anger, Arist.Po.1455a31: c. dat., to be angry with . . , Il.16.386, cf. Od.5.147, 16.114, 19.83; …

χαλεπότης.definition: difficulty, ruggedness; generally, difficulty, of understanding, Arist.APo.93b34

χαλέπτω.definition: poet. aor. Dosiad.Ara13:—Med. and; wound, Dosiad. l.c

χαλίκωμα.definition: in pl., rubble and mortar, concrete, Lat. caementa, Gloss

χαλιναγωγία.definition: guiding as by bit and bridle, Simp.in Epict.p.119D

χαλκεία.definition: smith's work, Hp.Art.53; opp; smithy, forge, HeroBel.98.3

χάλκειος.definition: Ep. for of copper or bronze; Subst., yellow fish thistle, Carlina corymbosa, Thphr.HP6.4.3, Plin.HN21.94

χάλκευμα.definition: anything made of brass, e.g. an; in pl., brazen bonds, Id.Pr.19

χαλκεύω.definition: make of copper or bronze or of

χαλκεών.definition: bar of wrought iron, Lat. strictura, glossed , Gloss

χαλκοθήκη.definition: a building on the Acropolis of Athens; case for bronze vessels, provided specially for those of value, Ath.6.231d

χαλκόμυια.definition: a fly of bright metallic hue, ingredient of an eye-salve, Aët.7.100

χαλκόω.definition: turn to bronze, AP9.795 :—Pass; clad in bronze, Pi.O.13.86

χαμαίδρυς.definition: germander, Teucrium Chamaedrys; = ib. III; also

χαμαίπιτυς.definition: ground-pine, Ajuga Chamaepitys; mountain germander, Teucrium montanum, Dsc. l. c., Plin. l.c

χαμευνάς.definition: on the ground, Lyc.848; = having their lair on the ground, Nonn.D.4.348, 6.299, 43.339

χαμεύνη.definition: for a bed on the ground; generally, bedstead, Ar.Av.816

χαμουλκός.definition: crane or windlass; Lat. = trahea, Gloss

χανδάνω.definition: Hp.Mul.1.78, Ep. impf. Il.23.742; in prescriptions, take, Nic.Th.956, Al.58,145

χαόω.definition: destroy utterly, swallow up, Simp.in Epict.p.47 D.:—Pass., Olymp.in Mete.143.5

χαράδρα.definition: Ion. mountain-stream, torrent; metaph. of wounds produced by scourging, Lib.Or.57.16

χαρακίζω.definition: fence with stakes driven in cross-wise: metaph. of a fly, dress itself by crossing the forelegs, Arist.PA683a30

χαρακίτης.definition: living behind a fence; = II, Afric.Cest.p.81 V., Aët.1.397

χαρακόω.definition: fence by a palisade, fortify; abs., raise a barricade against it, besiege it, LXXJe.39.2

χαρίσιος.definition: of thanksgiving; free, free gifts, Dam.Isid.216

χαρισμός.definition: bestowing of favours, gratifying, Sopat.inRh.8.70 W

χάρτης.definition: = foreg., papyrus, or a roll made; metaph., any leaf or thin plate, sheets of lead, Lysim. ap. J.Ap.1.34

χασκάζω.definition: Frequentat. of keep gaping at or after him, Ar.V.695

χάσκω.definition: Anacr.14.8, Ar.V.1493 ; subj; after Hom., gape in eager expectation, Sol.l.c.: freq. in Com., when I was all agape, Ar.Ach.10; the wolf opened his mouth , prov. of disappointed hopes, Id.Fr.337, cf. Eub.15.11, Euphro1…

χασμάομαι.definition: yawn, gape, when you are; = gabies, Porph.Chr.49

χάσμη.definition: yawning, gaping, Hp.Aph.7.56; esp. from; object of idle gaping, gazing-stock, Antip.Stoic.3.254

χασμωδέω.definition: write verses that have hiatus, Eust.11.42

χατέω.definition: Ep. Verb, used by Hom. only in pres.: later; c. gen., want, have need of, 3.48; Epic.Oxy.422, cf. AP5.301.20 , 7.583 , etc

χατίζω.definition: = foreg., only in pres., have need of, crave; lack, be without, i. e. to be idle, ib.21; a diet most defective in these elements, Hp.Morb.4.39

χαυνόω.definition: make flaccid, relax:—Pass., to become so; Pass., of inflammation, subside, Alex.Trall.3.3

χαύνωσις.definition: making slack or loose, opp; void space or interval, Gp.10.75.17

χάω.definition: contr. = coined as etym. of by Simp.in Ph.620.14

χειμαίνω.definition: aor. 1 , drive by a; metaph., disturb as by a storm, he who is himself in distress brings others into a like state, Arist.Po.1455a31; AP12.157

χειμίη.definition: Ion. for winter cold, chilly weather, ib.10

χειραλγός.definition: suffering from gout in the hand, Petr.Patr. in Boissevain D.C. iii p.744 No.166

χειριδόομαι.definition: Pass., to be furnished with hands; to be furnished with sleeves, Gloss

χείρισμα.definition: part handled or operated upon; treatment, ib.14,42

χειροδίκης.definition: one who asserts his right by hand, uses the right of might, Hes.Op.[189]

χειροκόπος.definition: cutting off the hands, Macr.Exc.p.601 K

χειροσκοπία.definition: vote by show of hands, Revue de l'histoire des religions63.331

χείρωμα.definition: that which is subdued, a conquest; deed of violence, S.OT560

χειρῶναξ.definition: one who is master of; generally, one who handles, deals in a thing, . . i.e. soothsayers, E.Fr.795.3

χερμάς.definition: large pebble or stone, esp. for; in later Poets, large block of stone, Lyc.20, 616, AP7.371

χερνίπτομαι.definition: fut. E.IT622: Med; sprinkle with holy water, purify or dedicate thereby, E.l.c

χερσεύω.definition: intr., abide on dry land, live or lie; to be dry land, opp. Arist.Mete.352a23

χέω.definition: used in the simple form mostly by Poets, but v; prop. of liquids, pour out, let flow, Il.9.15; 3.270, cf. Od.1.146, etc.; Il.23.220; Theoc.7.82: of Zeus, i.e. makes it rain, Il.16.385; . . E.Cyc.328: abs., it snows, I…

χηλόω.definition: notch arrows, Ph.Bel.77.8:—Pass., of a hook, to be equipped with claws, HeroBel.111.1

χηνέρως.definition: a small kind of goose, Plin.HN 10.56

χηνιάζω.definition: cackle like a goose, of a bad flute-player, Diph.77

χήρα.definition: Ion. widow, Il.2.289; Com., of a dish, widowed, i.e. without sauce, Sotad.Com.1.26

χηραίνω.definition: to be parted from one's husband, Herod.1.21

χηρεύω.definition: intr., to be without, lack, c. gen; abs. of a woman, to be widowed, live in widowhood, Is.6.51, D.30.11, 33; of birds, Arist.Fr.347; also of men, to be a widower, Plu.Cat.Ma.24:—Med., E.Alc.1089

χηρόω.definition: make desolate, Il.5.642: esp; c. gen., bereave, . . AP7.172 ; ib.287 :— Pass., . . Thgn.956; would have been bereft of . . , Sol.37; Hdt.6.83

χιασμός.definition: placing crosswise, diagonal arrangement; cruciform incision, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.20.32

χιλεύω.definition: supply with fodder, Thphr.CP2.17.6; feed on, graze, c. acc. loci, Nic.Th.635

χιλιαστύς.definition: a division of the people at Ephesus, ib.353.9 ; at Samos, ib.312.30 ; at Cos, ib.1025.17 ; cf

χιλιέτης.definition: celebration of the thousandth anniversary of the founding of Rome, IG22.3169.14

χιόνεος.definition: snowy, snow-white; of or from snow, Lyr.Alex.Adesp.37.12; AP9.244 ; ib.753 . by nature, but metri gr. in hexam.]

χιόω.definition: mark with a or cross, Tz.H.5.164; write or mark crosswise, Lyd.Mens.3.4: pf. inf. Eun.Hist.p.272D

χλαινόω.definition: cover with a cloak, AP9.293 : generally, clothe, Nonn.D.1.373

χλαίνωμα.definition: clothing, the lion's skin cloak, APl.4.104

χλιάω.definition: to be warm, in Ep. part., Nic.Al.110 Id.Fr.68.8 ; dub. sens. in Hesperia 5.95

χλιδιάω.definition: Desiderat., wish to be luxurious, cj. Lobeck for in Com.Adesp.1038

χλοάζω.definition: to be bright green, Arist.Mir.846b13; sprout, bud, Nic.Th.576; ib.917

χλωρίζω.definition: to be greenish or pale, LXXLe.13.49, 14.37; Herm.Trism. in Rev.Phil.32.258, cf. Aët.4.9

χλωρίς.definition: greenfinch, Fringilla chloris; a kind of grape, Gp.5.2.4

χλωρίων.definition: golden oriole, Oriolus galbula, Arist.HA616b11, 617a28, Plin.HN10.87

χνοάζω.definition: prop. of youths, get the first down; just sprinkling his hair with white, S.OT742

χόανος.definition: hollow in which metal was placed for; poet. for II, mould for casting metal in, Anacr.116

χολάς.definition: commonly in pl. bowels, guts; in sg., gut-cavity, common to the and Arist.HA493a21

χολάω.definition: to be full of black bile, to be; = to be angry, rage, Antiph.334, D.L.9.66, v.l. in Mosch.1.10, LXX3 Ma.3.1; Ep. part. Nic.Th.140

χολέρα.definition: Ion. cholera, a disease in which; obstinate obstruction, Hp.Acut..48. , but fr. Alex.Trall.8.1.)

χόλος.definition: rarely in physical sense; bitterness, Sol.4.39

χολόω.definition: inf. fut. Il.1.78: aor.1; Med. and Pass. ; 3sg. opt. Thgn.325 : fut. E.Tr.735; but in Hom. mostly Il.5.421, al.: aor. Med. and Pass. , Ep. Hom. , etc.: pf. mostly in part. v. infr.: plpf. 2 and 3sg. Il.16.585, 21.146;…

χονδριάω.definition: of women's breasts, swell with clots of milk, Dsc.2.107

χοοπότης.definition: one who drinks whole of Dionysus, Possis1

χοραυλέω.definition: accompany the chorus on the flute, Str.17.1.11

χορδεύω.definition: make into sausages: metaph., make mince-meat of state-affairs, ib.214

χορεῖος.definition: of or belonging to a chorus or dance; in metre, = Cic.de Or.3.50.193, Plu.2.1141b

χορηγίς.definition: woman-choragus, title of a Comedy by Alexis

χορτασία.definition: being fed, fullness; being fed, AP11.313

χόρτασμα.definition: mostly in pl., fodder, forage, for; food for men, Act.Ap.7.11

χορτοτομία.definition: a cutting of grass for hay, Gloss

χόω.definition: block up by throwing earth in, D.25.84, cf. Aeschin.3.109 ; Plb.1.19.13:—Pass., to be filled with earth, esp. of bays in the sea, to be silted up, Emp.100.17; . . Hdt.2.11; but of cities, to be raised on mounds, ib.137

χραισμέω.definition: Ep. Verb , pres. only in; more freq. c. dat. pers. only, defend, succour , freq. in Il.,1.28, 5.53, al.: c. neut. Adj., assist, avail at all, 1.242, 21.193, al.; abs., 14.66, 15.652.—Hom. uses with negs. expressed or …

χράω.definition: used in Ep. only in aor. 2, fall upon; c. acc. rei, inflict upon a person, Nic.Th.315

χρεμετίζω.definition: neigh, whinny, of horses, Il.12.51, Hdt.3.86,87, Pl.R.396b, Phdr.254d, Jul.Mis.366a: metaph. of lewd men, LXXJe.5.8.-In Hes.Sc.348 we have a shorter form of 3pl. aor. 1, asif from

χρῄζω.definition: c. acc. pers. et inf., ask or desire that one should do a thing, Hdt.1.41, 112, 152, al.; so c. gen. pers. et inf., desire of one to do, Id.5.19,65, 9.55; in Trag., c. inf. only, desire to do a thing, A.Pr.235, 285, a…

χρίμπτω.definition: bring near; Act. in Hom. only in compd; intr. in Act., Id.Ion156 ; Id.Andr.530 : abs., A.R.3.1286

χρίω.definition: rub, anoint with scented unguents or oil, as was done after bathing, freq. in Hom., Od.4.252; 3.466; 19.320; of a dead body, Il.23.186; anoint a suppliant, Berl.Sitzb.1927.170 ; rub or infect with poison, S.Tr.675, cf…

χροΐζω.definition: = touch the surface of a body, and; colour, stain, Dsc.2.80; poet. aor. Pass. Nic.Fr.74.26, cf. Gal.17.275

χρύσαμμος.definition: golden sand, Olymp.Alch.p.98 B.; = balluca, Gloss

χρυσανθής.definition: with flower of gold, Trag.Adesp; yellow dye, PHolm.22.2

χρυσίζω.definition: to be golden or like gold, Dsc.1.15, Crito; abound in gold, Arist.Mir.833b8

χρυσόμορφος.definition: in the likeness of gold, of Zeus descending to Danaë, S.Fr.[1127.2]

χρυσοποιία.definition: the making of gold, Syn.Alch.p.61B, Zos.Alch.p.220B

χρυσόχειρ.definition: with gold on the hands, i.e. with gold rings, Luc.Tim.20

χρωτίζω.definition: colour, give it colour and flavour, Plu.2.693c:—Med., tinge one's nature with . . , Ar.Nu.516

χυλίζω.definition: extract the juice from a plant by infusion or decoction, Dsc.Praef.9:—Pass., Thphr.HP9.9.4, cf. Dsc.2.182, etc

χυλισμός.definition: extraction of the juice of plants, Thphr.HP9.8.3

χυλόω.definition: convert into juice, make a decoction or; to be moistened, Eust.1552.33

χύλωσις.definition: converting into juice or chyle; thickening of a juice by decoction, Dsc.2.86, 109

χυμίζω.definition: make savoury, season: metaph., soften rough music, Ar.Th.162

χυμός.definition: used much like though sts; juice of plants, Hp.Epid.6.6.3 .327), Pl.Ti.60a, 60b, Arist.HA554a13, 596b17, Thphr.HP9.1.1, al

χύνω.definition: later form for found in compds.; condemned by Luc.Pseudol.29; also Gloss

χυτλόω.definition: wash, bathe, Id.322:—also in; Med., anoint oneself after bathing, Od.6.80: Medic., to rub oneself with a mixture of water and oil , Gal.11.532

χυτρῖνος.definition: deep hole from which water springs; niche for a nest in a dove-cot, in form Gp.14.6.2

χυτροτομέω.definition: make a fool of, dub. in Arg.Ar.Lys

χώλανσις.definition: lameness, Epict.Ench.9: metaph., in metric, of a halting line, Eust.400.3

χωλεύω.definition: to be or become lame, halt, limp; metaph., to be maimed, i. e. defective, imperfect, Plot.1.7.3; Lib.Or.47.10, cf. 59.33, Max.Tyr.20.6, Them.Or.6.75d; Palaeph.50; Gal.15.396

χωνεία.definition: melting and casting of metal, Plb.34.10.12, D.S.5.13

χώομαι.definition: Ep. imper. v. infr.: Ep. impf; c. dat. pers., to be angry at one, Il.1.80, al

χωρέω.definition: Anacr.108, etc.; fut. Il.16.629, Hdt.5.89, Hp.Nat.Puer.18, and in later Prose, as D.H.4.9, Luc.DDeor.20.15, etc.; Att. only in Th.1.82 ; elsewh. in Trag. and Att. always in med. form, A.Th.476, S.El.404, Th.2.20, etc.…

χώρησις.definition: a going, proceeding, =; Math., progression, Theol.Ar.34

χά.definition: exclamation representing laughter, ha! ha!, PMag.Leid.W.4.33

χερσόθεν.definition: Adv. from dry land, opp. sea, E.Heracl.429; from the ground, opp. water, Pi.O.2.73

χιαστί.definition: Adv. like the Chians, Eust.1462.34; crosswise, diagonally, Procl.in Euc.p.357 F

χορόνδε.definition: Adv. to the festive dance, Il.3.393

χωρίς.definition: Adv., also q. v.: :—separately; metaph., of different nature, kind, or quality, Semon.7.1; E.Alc.528; S.OC808; Pl.Prt.336b
